main.title: Pluto's reclassification
main.summary: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006 when astronomers adopted new criteria defining a planet.

cards.heading: Pluto's reclassification
cards.text:
Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006 when astronomers adopted new criteria defining a planet. It lies in the Kuiper belt beyond Neptune and is made mainly of ice and rock. With around one-sixth of the Moon's mass and one-third of its volume, it remains one of the largest known bodies in that region.

Its inclined, eccentric orbit carries it between roughly 30 and 49 astronomical units from the Sun. At its average distance, sunlight takes about five and a half hours to arrive. The orbit sometimes brings Pluto closer to the Sun than Neptune, while a stable orbital resonance keeps their paths from producing a collision.

cards.heading: Twitter
cards.text:
The platform was created in March 2006 by Jack Dorsey, Noah Glass, Biz Stone, and Evan Williams, and was launched in July of that year; initially named twttr, it was renamed Twitter some months later.

A signature characteristic of the service initially was that posts were required to be brief. Posts were initially limited to 140 characters.

main.title: V for Vendetta
main.summary: James McTeigue adapts Alan Moore and David Lloyd's comic into a dystopian thriller about fear, propaganda and resistance.

cards.heading: A mask against the state
cards.text: V for Vendetta is a 2006 dystopian thriller directed by James McTeigue, adapted by Lana and Lilly Wachowski from Alan Moore and David Lloyd's comic. In a future Britain ruled through fear and surveillance, Evey, played by Natalie Portman, encounters Hugo Weaving's masked insurgent V.

cards.heading: Resistance as spectacle
cards.text: V turns resistance into public theatre: a broadcast interrupts official propaganda, the Guy Fawkes mask conceals his identity, and the fifth of November gives his campaign a deadline. Evey's growing involvement places a personal story inside the struggle over who controls the country's images, voices and memory.

main.title: The Lives of Others
main.subtitle: An officer begins listening differently to the people he monitors
main.summary: Florian Henckel von Donnersmarck's The Lives of Others places a surveillance operation inside East Berlin in 1984. Ulrich Mühe plays Gerd Wiesler, a Stasi officer assigned to monitor playwright Georg Dreyman and actress Christa-Maria Sieland. Released in Germany on 23 March 2006, the film follows the effect that sustained listening has on the man responsible for turning private life into official evidence.

cards.heading: An apartment under observation
cards.text: Florian Henckel von Donnersmarck's The Lives of Others places a surveillance operation inside East Berlin in 1984. Ulrich Mühe plays Gerd Wiesler, a Stasi officer assigned to monitor playwright Georg Dreyman and actress Christa-Maria Sieland. Released in Germany on 23 March 2006, the film follows the effect that sustained listening has on the man responsible for turning private life into official evidence.

cards.heading: Listening and reporting
cards.text: Wiesler initially approaches the assignment as a skilled professional. Microphones, headphones and written reports give other people's rooms a second existence inside the security apparatus. The operation's political justification conceals a government official's personal interest in Christa-Maria. As Wiesler hears conversations and music beyond that purpose, his work becomes less mechanical. The tension depends on small decisions about what to record, what to report and how much danger a change in a document can create.

cards.heading: What remains in the records
cards.text: The film connects this hidden work with the pressures inside the apartment. Dreyman and Christa-Maria must judge whom they can trust, while Wiesler occupies a position that allows intimacy without reciprocal knowledge. Sebastian Koch and Martina Gedeck give those uncertain relationships their visible life; Mühe often has only a still face and a listening posture. Later scenes after reunification let the surviving records acquire a different meaning. The film won the 2007 foreign-language Oscar.

main.title: iPhone
main.summary: The iPhone is a smartphone developed and marketed by Apple as the first device in the iPhone lineup of smartphones.

cards.heading: iPhone
cards.text:
The iPhone is a smartphone developed and marketed by Apple as the first device in the iPhone lineup of smartphones. It features a Samsung S5L8900 SoC (90 nm), a 3.5 in multi-touch display, and a web browser (Safari). After years of rumors and speculation, it was officially announced on January 9, 2007, and was released in the United States on June 29, 2007.

Development of the iPhone began in 2005 and continued in secrecy until its public unveiling at Macworld 2007. The device broke with prevailing mobile phone designs by eliminating most physical hardware buttons, and relying on a finger-friendly touchscreen interface that did not need a stylus. The iPhone featured quad-band GSM cellular connectivity with GPRS and EDGE support for data transfer, and it used continuous internet access and onboard processing to support features unrelated to voice communication.

main.title: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix
main.subtitle: An unofficial classroom becomes a place of resistance
main.summary: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix turns the school into a contest over who is allowed to define the danger outside it. Harry knows Voldemort has returned, but the Ministry challenges his account and sends Dolores Umbridge to Hogwarts. David Yates directs the fifth film, with Imelda Staunton as the new teacher whose reassuring manners accompany increasingly severe restrictions. Michael Goldenberg adapted the novel for the screen. The film opened in the United States on 11 July 2007, a day before its British release.

cards.heading: A school that refuses to listen
cards.text: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix turns the school into a contest over who is allowed to define the danger outside it. Harry knows Voldemort has returned, but the Ministry challenges his account and sends Dolores Umbridge to Hogwarts. David Yates directs the fifth film, with Imelda Staunton as the new teacher whose reassuring manners accompany increasingly severe restrictions. Michael Goldenberg adapted the novel for the screen. The film opened in the United States on 11 July 2007, a day before its British release.

cards.heading: Learning behind closed doors
cards.text: Umbridge's refusal to teach practical defensive magic leads Harry and his friends to form their own training group. The Room of Requirement provides a space where students can practise spells, make mistakes and learn to trust one another. The growing confidence of that group gives the film a counterpoint to the Ministry's public denials and the punishment imposed inside the school. Nicholas Hooper's Dumbledore's Army accompanies this shared progress, while Harry's increasingly intrusive connection to Voldemort makes the question of whose judgement to trust more difficult for him personally.

main.title: Mad Men
main.subtitle: The people selling an ideal life struggle to arrange their own
main.summary: Matthew Weiner's Mad Men begins in a New York advertising agency in 1960. Jon Hamm plays Don Draper, a creative director skilled at giving products an emotional promise, while Elisabeth Moss plays newcomer Peggy Olson. The series premiered on AMC in the United States on 19 July 2007, placing professional ambition and private identity inside a workplace being changed by the decade around it.

cards.heading: An agency at the start of the sixties
cards.text: Matthew Weiner's Mad Men begins in a New York advertising agency in 1960. Jon Hamm plays Don Draper, a creative director skilled at giving products an emotional promise, while Elisabeth Moss plays newcomer Peggy Olson. The series premiered on AMC in the United States on 19 July 2007, placing professional ambition and private identity inside a workplace being changed by the decade around it.

cards.heading: Selling an emotional promise
cards.text: A presentation to a client can reveal more than the proposed campaign. Don's account of what people want often draws on needs he cannot settle in his own life. Peggy's arrival opens another route through the agency, where talent must negotiate assumptions about who may hold authority. Meetings, desks and office doors mark distinctions that can change slowly or suddenly. The work gives the ensemble a shared daily setting without making their prospects equal.

cards.heading: Change inside familiar rooms
cards.text: Costume, interiors and the language of advertising locate the characters in a recognisable period, but the series finds much of its drama in small changes of behaviour. A promotion or a new account can rearrange relationships that seemed stable. Events outside the office enter homes and conversations at different speeds. Returning to the same people across years lets the audience notice the distance between an image they have learned to present and the lives they are actually leading.

main.title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows
main.subtitle: The final book takes Harry, Ron and Hermione beyond school
main.summary: Harry, Ron and Hermione leave behind the familiar routine of Hogwarts to seek the objects on which Voldemort's survival depends. With places of refuge becoming unsafe, the search involves concealment, uncertain clues and long stretches without clear progress. Their friendship has to withstand exhaustion and disagreement as well as pursuit. Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows was published on 21 July 2007, completing the sequence J.K. Rowling had begun ten years earlier with The Philosopher's Stone.

cards.heading: Beyond the school year
cards.text: Harry, Ron and Hermione leave behind the familiar routine of Hogwarts to seek the objects on which Voldemort's survival depends. With places of refuge becoming unsafe, the search involves concealment, uncertain clues and long stretches without clear progress. Their friendship has to withstand exhaustion and disagreement as well as pursuit. Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows was published on 21 July 2007, completing the sequence J.K. Rowling had begun ten years earlier with The Philosopher's Stone.

cards.heading: Finishing a seven-book story
cards.text: The change of setting gives earlier discoveries a new use. Stories, inherited objects and fragments of personal history become evidence the three friends must interpret without the regular guidance of teachers. Questions about Dumbledore's past unsettle Harry's understanding of someone he had trusted, while the tale associated with the Hallows introduces another possible route through the conflict. The book gathers these threads towards a conclusion, asking its characters to decide what to pursue, whom to believe and what they are prepared to risk for one another.

main.title: In Rainbows
main.summary: Radiohead released In Rainbows as a download on 10 October 2007, inviting listeners to choose their own price.

cards.heading: In Rainbows
cards.text: Radiohead released In Rainbows as a download on 10 October 2007, inviting listeners to choose their own price. The band used its website to bypass a conventional promotional campaign after its contract with EMI had ended. Recording had begun in 2005; sessions with Spike Stent were followed by renewed work with longtime producer Nigel Godrich. The songs took a more personal lyrical direction than earlier records. A retail edition followed later in 2007. The initial release drew international attention to a major band's experiment with how an album could reach its audience.

main.title: Amazon Kindle
main.summary: Amazon Kindle is a series of e-readers designed and marketed by Amazon.

cards.heading: Amazon Kindle
cards.text: Amazon Kindle is a series of e-readers designed and marketed by Amazon. Amazon Kindle devices enable users to browse, buy, download, and read e-books, newspapers, magazines,  Audible audiobooks, and other digital media via wireless networking to the Kindle Store. The hardware platform, which Amazon subsidiary Lab126 developed, began as a single device in 2007. Currently, it comprises a range of devices, including e-readers with E Ink electronic paper displays and Kindle applications on all major computing platforms. All Kindle devices integrate with Windows and macOS file systems and Kindle Store content and, as of March 2018, the store had over six million e-books available in the United States.
